name: Room Pulse
notes:
Port of `room_pulse`: the whole strip lit, its level a raised cosine that peaks once per lap, resting at `tail` between. The previous port was a line travelling along the strip, which is what a chase looks like from OUTSIDE the room -- this animation is one light's share of that chase, and one light's share is a whole strip brightening and dimming.

The pulse is `lfo(ramp_up) -> envelope`, not a sine on opacity. A sine spends the whole cycle somewhere, and `width` exists precisely so the pulse can be NARROWER than its cycle. An LFO fires on its phase wrap, so it is the lap clock, and a `smooth` envelope with equal attack and decay is a symmetric raised bump of exactly the length asked for -- smootherstep either side, which is the raised cosine to within a hair.

`width` IS IN SECONDS HERE AND IN CYCLES THERE. The animation's width is a fraction of a lap, so it holds its duty ratio when `freq` changes; an envelope's attack and decay are seconds, and nothing scales one parameter by the reciprocal of another. Turning `freq` up therefore widens the duty rather than keeping it, and past about 1.4 Hz the default pulse no longer fits inside a lap.

COLOUR ADVANCES BUT DOES NOT STEP. The animation walks one palette entry per lap, counting visits off the room clock; nothing here counts, so a slow ramp at a quarter of the lap rate glides `paletteOffset` through the four entries once every four laps, with `wrap` on so the seam blends instead of snapping. The sequence is the same; the staircase is not.

AND THE POINT OF THE ANIMATION DOES NOT PORT AT ALL. `room_pulse` exists so several strips run one animation in step off `MeshClock`, a chase set up by a single broadcast with nothing to drop. There is no room-clock source (LIFE-676), so two devices running this drift apart and it is simply a pulsing light -- which is, to be fair, exactly what the animation degrades to on a device that has never heard a Master.
